findings.title: Untrusted upload type reaches a shell command
findings.body: `type` comes directly from the request and is included in the tempfile prefix for API URL uploads. This call passes that tempfile path to `OptimizedImage.downsize`, whose optimizer interpolates paths into a backtick shell command without escaping. An API caller can supply shell metacharacters in `type` and an oversized image URL, causing arbitrary commands to run as the application process. Restrict `type` to known values and invoke the image tool with safely escaped arguments or an argv array.

findings.title: The new definition overwrites the existing downsize signature
findings.body: Ruby does not overload methods, so this definition replaces the preceding `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`. Existing callers using that width/height form now fail: five arguments raise an arity error, while four arguments bind `max_height` as `opts` and later fail when it is indexed by `:force_aspect_ratio`. Preserve the old call form in a single method or update all callers.

findings.title: Upload validation no longer honors the attachment size setting
findings.body: This validator handles both images and attachments, but the fixed 10 MB limit replaces the per-type site setting. Attachments above a configured lower `max_attachment_size_kb` are now sent to the server only to be rejected there, while valid attachments cannot be selected when the configured limit is above 10 MB. Keep attachment validation tied to its configured limit and use a separate raw-upload cap for images that will be downsized.

findings.title: Five resize attempts can still leave an image over the configured limit
findings.body: The loop stops after five 80% dimension reductions even if the file remains larger than `max_image_size_kb`; the upload then reaches `Upload.create_for` and is rejected. For example, a high-entropy 10 MB PNG reduced by 80% in each dimension retains about 64% of its size per pass, leaving roughly 1.07 MB after five passes against a 1 MB limit. Continue resizing until the limit is met or report that downsizing failed.
